summary: A statement of policy from the Internet Activities Board on the proper use of Internet resources. It is a short policy statement and not a technical specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This Internet Activities Board memo states that users share responsibility for protecting Internet resources. It names harmful activities and urges caution with experiments that could affect other users.

subtitle: The Internet Activities Board's policy on responsible use of Internet resources.

tldr.problem: The Internet depends on shared resources, and irresponsible use can threaten its availability and the work it supports.
tldr.mechanism: The Internet Activities Board identifies activities it considers unethical, including unauthorized access, disruption, waste, damage to information and privacy violations.
tldr.outcome: The memo places responsibility for protecting the Internet's health on its users. Its status is listed as Unknown.

sections.title: Why Responsible Use Matters
sections.content: The Internet Activities Board (IAB) issued this policy statement because many users depend on the Internet for research and other work. The memo describes the Internet as a shared infrastructure built with government, industry and academic resources. It says reliable operation and responsible use are matters of common concern for users, operators and sponsors.
sections.plainLanguage: Many people depend on the Internet, and they share its resources. The IAB says responsible use helps keep those resources available.

sections.title: Activities the IAB Condemns
sections.content: The IAB endorses the view that it is unethical and unacceptable to purposely seek unauthorized access to Internet resources, disrupt the Internet's intended use, waste people or system capacity through such actions, destroy the integrity of computer-based information, or compromise users' privacy. Researchers also have a responsibility to use great caution because Internet-wide experiments can affect many components and users.
sections.plainLanguage: The IAB condemns deliberate break-ins, disruption, waste, damage to information and invasions of privacy. Researchers should take care because an experiment can affect other parts of the Internet.

sections.title: Users Share Responsibility
sections.content: The memo describes access to and use of the Internet as a privilege. It says the IAB plans to work with government agencies and other interested parties on technical and procedural ways to resist disruption. It also warns that security measures may be expensive and could hinder the free flow of information, and concludes that users must guard against abuse that threatens the Internet's long-term viability.
sections.plainLanguage: Users must help protect the network from abuse. The memo also says protection should not needlessly block the flow of information.
